testCases.input: how did mmlu pro improve on the original mmlu?
testCases.actualOutput:
MMLU Pro was built to push the original MMLU benchmark a step further. The first thing the designers did was make the multiple‑choice format harder: instead of the usual four answer choices, each question now offers ten. That extra set of distractors means a model can’t simply eliminate three wrong answers and be left with one; it has to sift through a larger pool, which raises the difficulty level.

At the same time, the creators trimmed the “easy” part of the dataset. They removed the most basic, noisy questions that had been part of the original MMLU and replaced them with items that demand more reasoning. In other words, the new benchmark focuses on questions that require the model to apply logic or deeper knowledge rather than just recall facts.

Because of these changes, the performance gap between models and humans narrows—models are now reaching human‑level scores on MMLU Pro, even though the paper didn’t publish a human baseline. In short, MMLU Pro improves on the original by giving each question ten options, dropping low‑quality items, and adding more reasoning‑heavy questions, thereby creating a more challenging and realistic test of a model’s abilities.
